title: Metabolic, nutritional and performance compounds
description: Vitamins and cofactors, amino acids and their derivatives, and small-molecule metabolic drugs, with the energy-sensing and metabolic enzyme targets they are discussed against.

compounds.name: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C)
compounds.notes: Redox cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases; the enediol is readily oxidised to dehydroascorbate in solution.

compounds.name: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3)
compounds.notes: Hydroxylated by CYP2R1 to 25-hydroxyvitamin D and then by CYP27B1 to the active 1,25-dihydroxy hormone.

compounds.name: Nicotinamide
compounds.notes: Salvage-pathway NAD+ precursor via nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase; also a product inhibitor of sirtuins and PARPs.

compounds.name: Nicotinic acid (niacin)
compounds.notes: Agonist of HCAR2 (GPR109A), which mediates the characteristic prostaglandin-driven flushing response.

compounds.name: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN)
compounds.notes: Direct NMNAT substrate one step from NAD+; its phosphate is dephosphorylated extracellularly before uptake.

compounds.name: Thiamine (vitamin B1)
compounds.notes: Precursor of thiamine pyrophosphate, the cofactor for pyruvate and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase and transketolase.

compounds.name: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6)
compounds.notes: Converted to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, the cofactor for transaminases and aromatic amino acid decarboxylase.

compounds.name: Folic acid
compounds.notes: Reduced by dihydrofolate reductase to tetrahydrofolate, the one-carbon carrier for thymidylate and methionine synthesis.

compounds.name: Creatine
compounds.notes: Phosphorylated by creatine kinase to phosphocreatine, buffering ATP resynthesis; cyclises non-enzymatically to creatinine.

compounds.name: L-Theanine
compounds.notes: Tea-derived glutamine analog hydrolysed by intestinal and renal glutaminase to glutamate and ethylamine.

compounds.name: Taurine
compounds.notes: Conjugates bile acids and contributes to cell-volume osmoregulation; not incorporated into proteins.

compounds.name: N-Acetylcysteine
compounds.notes: Deacetylated to cysteine and thereby replenishes glutathione, the basis of its use after acetaminophen overdose.

compounds.name: L-Carnitine
compounds.notes: Carries long-chain acyl groups across the inner mitochondrial membrane through the CPT1/CPT2 shuttle.

compounds.name: Beta-alanine
compounds.notes: Rate-limiting precursor of muscle carnosine; transient paraesthesia arises from MRGPRD activation.

compounds.name: L-Citrulline
compounds.notes: Converted to arginine in the kidney, raising plasma arginine more effectively than oral arginine itself.

compounds.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
compounds.notes: Covalently bound lipoamide cofactor of 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes; the free dithiolane is redox active and photolabile.

compounds.name: Metformin
compounds.notes: Highly hydrophilic cation taken up by OCT1/OCT2 and excreted unchanged renally; inhibits mitochondrial complex I with downstream AMPK activation.

compounds.name: Berberine
compounds.notes: Quaternary protoberberine alkaloid with low oral bioavailability and clinically relevant CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition.
